bug_description.normalized: OSS-Fuzz issue 35359: libvips has a reported memory-safety bug. A JPEG XL codestream is loaded through libvips' jpegsave_buffer_fuzzer and decoded by libjxl. AddressSanitizer reports a Container-overflow READ 8 at crash address 0x618000010340 with crash state jxl::DefaultSqueezeParameters / jxl::MetaSqueeze / jxl::Transform::MetaApply: the modular-image Squeeze transform indexes image.channel[nb_meta_channels] with no non-meta channel present, reading past the end of the channel vector.

source.description: The modular group header (the attacker-controlled transform list, including the Squeeze transform) is parsed from the untrusted JXL codestream. This is the project-level parse/materialization point that supplies the transform later applied to the modular image.
source.value_from: Untrusted JXL codestream bytes decoded into header.transforms (a kSqueeze transform) together with the modular image channel configuration (image.nb_meta_channels vs image.channel.size()).

sink.description: Container-overflow READ 8: DefaultSqueezeParameters reads the size_t .w field of image.channel[image.nb_meta_channels]. When the modular image has meta channels but zero non-meta channels, this index equals image.channel.size(), so the read lands one element past the end of the std::vector<Channel> (ASan container annotation region) at 0x618000010340.

root_cause.description: DefaultSqueezeParameters (and its caller MetaSqueeze) never verify that the modular image contains at least one non-meta channel (nb_channels >= 1, i.e. image.channel.size() > image.nb_meta_channels) before unconditionally indexing image.channel[image.nb_meta_channels]. A malformed JXL stream that carries a Squeeze transform on an image with only meta channels therefore drives an out-of-bounds container read. Note: the ARVO-recorded fix commit (libvips 6dd6fafa, adding an ENABLE_MODULES guard around vips_load_plugins) is a libvips build-configuration change that removes reachability of this libjxl decode path in the fuzzer regression; it does not itself add the missing channel-count validation in libjxl.

tainted_value_origin.description: The untrusted, decoded transform list (containing a kSqueeze transform) is copied into the modular image. Combined with a channel set that has no non-meta channel, this attacker-controlled transform is what steers execution into the out-of-bounds DefaultSqueezeParameters read.

parser_admitted.description: The input has been admitted as a JXL modular stream and entered ModularDecode with a non-empty channel set, so it proceeds to read and apply the codestream transforms (the path toward the Squeeze root cause / sink).

coarse_trace.summary: Reads the modular group header from the codestream and applies each decoded transform to the image.
Dispatches on the transform id; for kSqueeze it calls MetaSqueeze.
With an empty squeeze-parameter list, computes default squeeze parameters from the image geometry.
Reads image.channel[nb_meta_channels].w without checking a non-meta channel exists, overrunning the channel vector.

fine_trace.note: Scored source: the modular group header (including the attacker-controlled Squeeze transform) is parsed from the untrusted JXL codestream.
The decoded, attacker-controlled transform list is materialized into the modular image.
Each decoded transform is applied to the image via MetaApply.
Control: the transform id selects the kSqueeze branch (taken), dispatching into MetaSqueeze.
Control: the stream carried no explicit squeeze parameters, so the empty-list branch is taken (line 209) and DefaultSqueezeParameters is invoked to synthesize them.

Root cause: nb_channels can be <= 0 when the image has only meta channels, but the missing check `nb_channels < 1` is never performed before the channel is indexed. Control `via` names the guard that is absent (missing).

Sink (crash_location): with no non-meta channel present the index equals image.channel.size(), so reading the 8-byte size_t .w overruns the std::vector<Channel> -> ASan Container-overflow READ 8. Control `via` is the bounds guard that is missing.

sanitizer_ground_truth.source: OSS-Fuzz issue 35359 crash_state (authoritative). The local sanitizer_trace.txt captured on this host is an amd64-on-arm64 (Docker Desktop/QEMU) emulation artifact: a pre-main BUS (wild-addr-read) in heif::register_decoder via __sanitizer_cov_trace_pc_indir, PoC-independent and present on both vul and fix images. It does NOT reflect this vulnerability; crash semantics here are grounded in the OSS-Fuzz report plus the vulnerable source read from the arvo:35359-vul image.
sanitizer_ground_truth.note: reproduction_rate=0.0 and patch_resolves=false because the target could not be exercised on this arm64 host (needs a native x86_64 host). The recorded fix commit is a libvips build-config change (ENABLE_MODULES guard); it removes reachability of the buggy libjxl squeeze path rather than adding the missing channel-count validation in libjxl.

format.name: JPEG XL (JXL) codestream
format.contract: Candidate input must be admitted by libvips' JXL loader as a naked JXL codestream (signature 0xFF 0x0A) and decoded by libjxl's modular decoder far enough to carry a Squeeze (kSqueeze) transform applied to a modular image that has meta channels but zero non-meta channels (image.channel.size() == image.nb_meta_channels), so DefaultSqueezeParameters indexes image.channel[nb_meta_channels] out of bounds. Do not depend on original PoC bytes; any input preserving JXL parser-admission and this empty-non-meta-channel squeeze state is reachability-comparable.
